- scripts/heal_isolated_implement.sh:545-569 | severity=high | confidence=5

  PROBLEM: In cmd_final, when one listed test passes on the edited tree and another still fails, run 2 is skipped on purpose. The passing test then sets `unverified="not_run_at_failing_sha"`, and because `if unverified:` is checked before `elif mismatch:`, the outcome is reported as `unverified/not_run_at_failing_sha` instead of `not_fixed/still_failing`.
  WHY: The heal is still held with exit 43, but HEAL_REPRO_RESULT_FILE and the refusal comment record the wrong outcome and hide a definite still-failing test. This contradicts agents.d/heal-implement-repro-check.md, and every existing test uses a single test id, so nothing catches it. Severity disagrees: four reviewers rate it MAJOR and openai_gpt-6-luna rates it NIT; the highest is used.
- scripts/heal_isolated_implement.sh:604-621 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: heal_impl_repro_required looks for `[repro-required]` only on the first line (`split("\n")[0]`) of the comment that triggered this run, and the check is not tied to the approved plan. A trigger like `/approved\n[repro-required]`, or a later bare `/approved` re-approval, therefore prints `none` and skips the reproduction check.
  WHY: implement.yml line 108 accepts any body that starts with `/approved`. The unblock judge also posts a bare `/approved` after a `repro_not_fixed` needs-human hold (scripts/unblock_actions.py _approve, line 710, reached from lines 743-745). In both cases the edit is transferred and the PR opens without reproduction, which bypasses the fail-closed requirement. All three reviewers rate it MAJOR.
- scripts/heal_isolated_implement.sh:685-699 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: repro-tree is a fresh detached worktree at HEAD, but manifest.repro.json records the host baseline, including untracked and modified files. transfer() (scripts/review_untrusted_workspace.py:466-469) then raises "host baseline changed", and the failure path always exits 42, even though the host transfer would succeed.
  WHY: An in-scope heal is refused as `out_of_heal_scope` with `ai:needs-human`, and the reproduction result is never posted. By contrast, the gate tree handles the same failure fail-open (`gate_tree_unavailable`, lines 309-313). Suggested fix: route it to `heal_impl_repro_finish repro_tree_unavailable` (exit 43). Severity disagrees: three reviewers rate it MAJOR and openai_gpt-6-luna rates it NIT; the highest is used.
- scripts/heal_isolated_implement.sh:497-510 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: cmd_tests splits on every comma (`re.split(r"[,\s]+", match.group(1))`), which breaks valid parametrized pytest ids such as `tests/test_x.py::test_case[a,b]` into malformed fragments.
  WHY: The fragments fail PATH_RE/NAME_RE, so a valid plan is held as `plan_tests_unreadable` (exit 43), or the wrong id is reproduced, and the listed test is never checked. The gate's validator accepts such ids. This fails closed, so it causes a false hold, not a bypass. Severity disagrees: two reviewers rate it MAJOR and three rate it NIT; the highest is used.
- tests/test_heal_isolated_editor.py:1088 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: `f"--worktree "` is an f-string with no placeholders (ruff F541).
  WHY: The pre-push gate lists ruff among the failures this change causes, so the lint tier fails on the changed file. The fix is to drop the `f` prefix. Severity disagrees: google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite rates it MAJOR and the other four rate it NIT; the highest is used.

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/heal_isolated_implement.sh:heal_impl_repro_required, lines 604-621 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Whether reproduction is required is decided only from the first line of the comment that started this run (`split("\n")[0]`), not from the approved plan. A heal whose plan has `HEAL_COUNTERFACTUAL: REPRODUCIBLE:` skips the check whenever a re-approval lacks the marker on its first line.
  WHY: A `repro_not_fixed` refusal adds `ai:needs-human` (scripts/implement_heal_preflight.sh line 43). The unblock judge then posts a bare `/approved` (scripts/unblock_actions.py: _approve at line 710, reached from lines 743-745), so the next run gets `none` and the PR opens without reproduction. Separately, implement.yml line 108 only checks `startsWith(body, '/approved')`, so `/approved\n[repro-required]` also skips the check. Suggested fix: also report `required` when PLAN_FILE has exactly one unfenced `HEAL_COUNTERFACTUAL: REPRODUCIBLE:` line.
- scripts/heal_isolated_implement.sh:cmd_final in the embedded heal_impl_repro_py, around lines 545-569 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: With test A passing and test B still failing, run 2 is skipped. A then sets `unverified="not_run_at_failing_sha"`, B sets `mismatch="still_failing"`, and because `unverified` wins the outcome is `unverified/not_run_at_failing_sha`.
  WHY: heal_implement_repro.v1 records the wrong outcome and reason, which hides a definite still-failing test and contradicts the agents.d fragment. Every existing test uses a single test id. Suggested fix: `elif failing: unverified = unverified or "not_run_at_failing_sha"`.
- scripts/heal_isolated_implement.sh:heal_impl_repro_check, repro-tree transfer (`review_untrusted_workspace.py transfer "${root}/repro-tree" "${root}/source" "${root}/manifest.repro.json" --scope-file "${scope}" ...; then ... exit 42`) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: repro-tree is a clean checkout of HEAD, while the manifest baseline comes from snapshot() (scripts/review_untrusted_workspace.py lines 373-377, 418). transfer() (lines 466-469) raises "host baseline changed" when the host has untracked or modified baseline files.
  WHY: An in-scope heal exits 42 and is refused as `out_of_heal_scope` with `ai:needs-human` (implement.yml lines 3683-3685), so the wrong reason is posted. The gate tree handles this fail-open (lines 309-313, `gate_tree_unavailable`). Suggested fix: route it to `heal_impl_repro_finish repro_tree_unavailable "${failing_sha}"` (exit 43).
- tests/test_heal_isolated_editor.py:line 1088 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `f"--worktree "` is an f-string with no placeholders (ruff F541).
  WHY: The pre-push gate lists ruff among the failures, and this is the F-class violation. Fix: drop the `f` prefix.
- scripts/heal_isolated_implement.sh:cmd_tests `for raw in re.split(r"[,\s]+", match.group(1)):` | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Splitting on every comma breaks parametrized ids like `tests/test_x.py::test_case[a,b]`.
  WHY: The fragments fail NAME_RE/PATH_RE, so the heal is held as `plan_tests_unreadable` (exit 43). This is a false hold, not a bypass.
- HARDENING: scripts/heal_isolated_implement.sh:heal_prepush_test_gate, line 320 (`bash "${support}/codex_isolated_exec.sh" prepare --workdir ... --deps`)
  PROBLEM: The dependency prepare step has no time limit, yet the gate budget reserves 630 s for the transfer.
  WHY: Suggested fix: prefix the call with `timeout --kill-after=30s 600` (stays fail-open). About 1 line.
- HARDENING: scripts/heal_isolated_implement.sh:heal_impl_repro_check `rm -f -- "${root}/results/repro-edited.json" "${root}/results/repro-failing.json"`
  PROBLEM: The previous `${HEAL_REPRO_RESULT_FILE}` is never removed, and cmd_final only warns on OSError.
  WHY: The preflight could render an outdated result. Suggested fix: add `"${heal_impl_repro_result_file}"` to the `rm -f`. About 1 line.
- HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 2
